source_text: Quaeritur ergo a nobis, cur non assentiamur naturale esse peccatum. Respondemus: Quia nullum habet verisimilitudinis necdum veritatis, nullum iustitiae, nullum pietatis colorem, quia diabolum conditorem hominum facit videri.
pass_a_gloss: It is asked therefore of us why we do not assent that sin is natural. We answer: Because it has no color of likelihood, much less of truth, none of justice, none of piety, because it makes the devil seem the founder of humans.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: We are asked, then, why we do not agree that sin is natural. We answer: Because the idea has no appearance of plausibility, much less truth, no appearance of justice or piety; because it makes the devil appear to be humanity’s creator.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
